findings.title: XSum AI-text and prompt inputs absent; Table 2/3/4 not reproducible from shipped data
findings.claim: The default XSum run reads AI texts from ./txtdata/xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json and (white-box) prompts from ./txtdata/xsum_prompt.json (via get_prompt, detector.py:1021); txtdata/ ships only xsum_human.json — the AI-text and prompt files are absent.
findings.concern: The entire main experiment (Table 2/3/4, all on XSum) cannot be run from the shipped artifacts; regenerating the missing files requires generate_human_dataset.py + generate_ai_dataset.py, i.e. network access, the gated meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf model, and the HuggingFace XSum dataset, none noted in the README.
findings.resolution: Commit xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json and xsum_prompt.json (the exact 200 samples used), or document the regeneration steps and pin dataset/model revisions and seeds.

findings.title: README instructs running detection_binoculars_only.py, which is absent
findings.claim: README step 2 tells users to run `python detection_binoculars_only.py`; no such file exists in the repo (the working mechanism is `python detection.py --binoculars_only`).
findings.concern: Following the README verbatim fails with 'No such file or directory'; a reader cannot reproduce the Binoculars row without discovering the undocumented flag.
findings.resolution: Fix the README to `python detection.py --binoculars_only`, or add the referenced script.

findings.title: `prompt_label = idx` overrides AI-only branch: human texts get prompts; AI indices overflow prompt_list
findings.claim: Inside the white-box loop, `prompt_label = idx` executes unconditionally within `if is_prompt`, discarding the `idx - len(human_texts)` value the preceding `if label_list[idx]` branch just computed; prompt_label then equals idx for every sample.
findings.concern: In plain white-box mode (`--prompt`, the mode that produced Table 2 — the committed file has no `_self_prompt` tag) prompt_list holds one prompt per AI sample (len == datasize), so (a) human texts (idx < datasize) get a prompt prepended, contradicting §4.2 ('For human-generated text, only x is input'), and (b) every AI text (idx >= datasize) indexes prompt_list out of range, raising IndexError at the first AI sample — the headline white-box column cannot be produced by the shipped code. The override is the `--self_prompt` indexing (prompt_list len == 2*datasize) leaking into plain mode.
findings.resolution: Remove line 984 (`prompt_label = idx`) so the AI-only branch stands (human -> -1, AI -> idx-len(human_texts)), or gate it behind `if self_prompt`; confirm which indexing produced the committed white-box results.
findings.paper_ref: Section 4.2 Detection methods; Table 2 White-box column

findings.title: evaluation.py has an unclosed call — the file does not compile
findings.claim: Line 26's random.sample(...) call is never closed and omits the sample-size argument; `python -m py_compile evaluation.py` fails with `SyntaxError: '(' was never closed` (see _audit_code/out — reproduced during the audit).
findings.concern: evaluation.py cannot be imported or run at all; it computes a BERTScore between AI and human estimated-prompt texts (a prompt-estimation quality check), so no Table 2/3/4 number depends on it, hence low severity — but it is definitively broken.
findings.resolution: Close the call and supply the size argument, e.g. `random.sample(list(human_prompt_texts.values()), size)`.

findings.title: Binoculars uses OpenLLaMA-3B in code, not the paper's Phi-1.5
findings.quote:
observer_name_or_path: str = "tiiuae/falcon-7b"
            performer_name_or_path: str = "tiiuae/falcon-7b-instruct"

            observer_name_or_path = "01-ai/Yi-6B"
            performer_name_or_path = "HenryJJ/Instruct_Yi-6B_Dolly15K"

            observer_name_or_path = "openlm-research/open_llama_3b_v2"
            performer_name_or_path = "mediocredev/open-llama-3b-v2-instruct"
findings.claim: The Binoculars observer/performer are reassigned three times; the last assignment wins, so the code runs OpenLLaMA-3B (`openlm-research/open_llama_3b_v2` / `mediocredev/open-llama-3b-v2-instruct`).
findings.concern: Paper §5.1 states 'Binoculars employs the pre-trained and instruct-tuned Phi1.5 [27] instead of Falcon'; neither the effective OpenLLaMA-3B pair nor the dead Falcon/Yi options is Phi-1.5, so the Binoculars row of Table 2 (0.877/0.999) was produced with a different model than reported.
findings.resolution: State which model pair produced the reported Binoculars numbers and reconcile the code with §5.1 (either restore Phi-1.5 or correct the paper).
findings.paper_ref: Section 5.1 Configuration ('Phi1.5 instead of Falcon'); Table 2 Binoculars row

findings.title: Committed results do not reproduce Table 2 for 6/10 detectors (3 white-box rows ≈ 1−paper)
findings.claim: Recomputing AUC from the committed results/*.json (paper_black, stored_black, recomputed_black, match, paper_white, stored_white, recomputed_white, match): the stored roc_auc differs from Table 2 by >0.02 for DetectGPT(W), LRR(B), NPR(B+W), Entropy(B+W), Log-likelihood(B), Rank(B+W), Log-Rank(B+W); for Entropy/Rank/Log-Rank the stored value ≈ 1 − paper in BOTH columns (score orientation inverted).
findings.concern: The exact Table 2 numbers are not reproduced by the shipped artifacts; the committed files use an older filename scheme and the current code cannot regenerate them (missing XSum inputs), and taken at face value 3 stored white-box rows (Entropy 0.022, Rank 0.023, Log-Rank 0.001) are below their black-box values, contradicting the abstract's 'white-box beats black-box by ≥0.1'.
findings.resolution: Provide the code+seed+data that produced Table 2, or refresh results/*.json; clarify the per-detector score orientation (sign convention) so AUCs are comparable to the table.

findings.title: Human class = short XSum reference summaries vs AI = up-to-200-token generations (length/verbosity confound)
findings.quote:
train_data = batch["document"][0]
            if len(train_data) < 1000 or len(train_data) >= 1500:
                continue
            human_txts[counter] = batch["summary"][0]
            context_txts[counter] = train_data
findings.claim: The human class is the XSum gold `summary` (median 20 words / 123 chars over the 200 shipped samples; the 1000–1500-char length filter is applied to the source `document`, not the summary), while the AI class is a Llama-2 summary generated 'up to 200 tokens' (§5.1).
findings.concern: The two classes differ systematically in length and register (terse reference summary vs verbose chat output), so a detector may separate them partly via a length/verbosity shortcut rather than a pure human-vs-AI likelihood signal; the paper reports no length-matched or per-length breakdown. (Confidence low: the AI file is absent so I could not measure the AI-side lengths, and this affects both black and white boxes, so the white−black delta is less affected.)
findings.resolution: Report the human vs AI length distributions and, ideally, a length-controlled evaluation (or truncate/match lengths) to show the effect is not a length artefact.
findings.paper_ref: Section 5.1 ('extract 200 samples from the XSum dataset'; 'generating up to 200 tokens')
